newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Gas oil, fuel oil swaps set to flip into contango.
newsitem.headline: Gas oil, fuel oil swaps set to flip into contango.

text.p: The lack of Chinese gas oil and fuel oil imports and a glut in prompt supplies are threatening to push both markets into contango, traders said on Thursday.
"This could be the start of a new era as we see the Korean barrels hitting the market," one refining source said.
"The market could end up trading in contango for the better part of 1997 as was the case two to three years ago," another trader said.

A market is in contango when prices in future months are higher than the forward month. For the better part of 1996, both the fuel oil and gas oil markets were backwardated, where price on the forward month is higher.
The February/March time spread for fuel oil is currently flat while gas oil traded at 5 cents.
Just over a week ago, the fuel oil February/March spread was valued at about $1.00 per tonne and gas oil valued at around 50 cents a barrel, brokers said.
Both markets are reeling from new South Korean refining capacity that is only now hitting the market as all the crude units operate are at full capacity.
In late December, LG-Caltex managed to operate a crude unit which has a goverment-licensed production capacity of 220,000 barrels per day (bpd).
Company officials said the crude distillation unit (CDU) is capable of processing 270,000-bpd of crude oil.
The second refiner, Yukong Ltd, in mid-October brought on line a new 200,000-bpd crude unit but at the same time shut down a 265,000-bpd unit for a 30-day maintenance.
Yukong, the nation's largest refiner with a 810,000 barrel-per-day capacity, was only operating all units at full capacity in December.

These two refineries, traders said, have contributed to the tremendous rise in spot gas oil and fuel oil spot exports from South Korea which is currently offering several cargoes of both productS for loading in February.

The prompt supply glut is exacerbated by poor Chinese demand. China had in the past few months supported the markets through record purchases but its purchases had slowed down considerably for February arrival cargoes.
A build up of stocks, improved refining runs and low demand due to the Lunar New Year holidays all combined to curtail Chinese imports, traders said.
As a result, fuel oil and gas oil stocks in Hong Kong are nearing tank top, they said. Traders usually sell 1,000-5,000 tonne barge lots of products from Hong Kong to southern China.
Traders also said that refiners in Singapore are now forced to store their oil in independent storage terminals due to the reduced regional demand.

While the gas oil supply glut is primarily driven by regional imbalances, the fuel oil situation is compounded by the export of arbitrage cargoes from the U.S. and Venezuela as well as several Middle East spot cargoes.
Traders said it would take at least another month before the market can absorb all the fuel oil exports from outside the region.
Players are hoping for Chinese demand to pick up after the holidays as that market is the only one that can absorb all the new capacities.
--Singapore Newsroom (+65-870-3093)
